paragraphs.en: dispersible granules the active ingredient content is, for example, between 1 and 95% by weight, preferably between 10 and 80% by weight.

paragraphs.zh: Daneben enthalten die genannten Wirkstoffformulierungen gegebenenfalls die jeweils üblichen Haft-, Netz-, Dispergier-, Emulgier-, Penetrations-, Konservierungs-, Frostschutz- und Lösungsmittel, Füll-, Träger- und Farbstoffe, Entschäumer, Verdunstungshemmer und den pH-Wert und die Viskosität beeinflussende Mittel.
paragraphs.en: In addition, the stated active ingredient formulations optionally contain the customary tackifiers, wetting agents, dispersants, emulsifiers, penetrants, preservatives, antifreeze agents and solvents, fillers, carriers and colorants, defoamers, evaporation inhibitors, and agents which influence the pH and the viscosity.
paragraphs.notes: The German uses a chain of clipped compounds sharing the head words 'mittel' and 'stoffe' (Haft-, Netz-, Dispergier-, Emulgier-, Penetrations-, Konservierungs-, Frostschutz- und Loesungsmittel; Fuell-, Traeger- und Farbstoffe). Transcribed with the hyphens exactly as printed. A small ink speck sits above this line in the scan; it is not a character.

paragraphs.zh: Als Kombinationspartner für die erfindungsgemäßen Wirkstoffe in Mischungsformulierungen oder im Tank-Mix sind beispielsweise bekannte Wirkstoffe einsetzbar, wie sie z.B. in Weed Research 26, 441-445 (1986) oder "The Pesticide Manual", 11th edition, The British Crop Protection Council and the Royal Soc. of Chemistry, 1997 und dort zitierter Literatur beschrieben sind. Als bekannte Herbizide, die mit den Verbindungen der Formel (I) kombiniert werden können, sind z.B. folgende Wirkstoffe zu nennen (Anmerkung: Die Verbindungen sind entweder mit dem "common name" nach der International Organization for Standardization (ISO) oder mit dem chemischen Namen, ggf. zusammen mit einer üblichen Codenummer bezeichnet):
paragraphs.en: As combination partners for the active compounds according to the invention in mixture formulations or in a tank mix, known active compounds can be used, for example those described in Weed Research 26, 441-445 (1986) or "The Pesticide Manual", 11th edition, The British Crop Protection Council and the Royal Soc. of Chemistry, 1997 and in the literature cited therein. Known herbicides which can be combined with the compounds of the formula (I) include, for example, the following active compounds (note: the compounds are designated either by the "common name" according to the International Organization for Standardization (ISO) or by the chemical name, where appropriate together with a customary code number):

paragraphs.en: acetochlor; acifluorfen; aclonifen; AKH 7088, i.e. [[[1-[5-[2-chloro-4-(trifluoromethyl)-phenoxy]-2-nitrophenyl]-2-methoxyethylidene]-amino]-oxy]-acetic acid and -acetic acid methyl ester; alachlor; alloxydim; ametryn; amidosulfuron; amitrol; AMS, i.e. ammonium sulfamate; anilofos; asulam; atrazine; azimsulfurone (DPX-A8947); aziprotryn; barban; BAS 516 H, i.e. 5-fluoro-2-phenyl-4H-3,1-benzoxazin-4-one; benazolin; benfluralin; benfuresate; bensulfuron-methyl; bensulide; bentazone; benzofenap; benzofluor; benzoylprop-ethyl; benzthiazuron; bialaphos; bifenox; bromacil; bromobutide; bromofenoxim; bromoxynil; bromuron; buminafos; busoxinone; butachlor; butamifos; butenachlor; buthidazole; butralin; butylate; cafenstrole (CH-900); carbetamide; cafentrazone (ICI-A0051); CDAA, i.e. 2-chloro-N,N-di-2-propenylacetamide; CDEC, i.e. 2-chloroallyl diethyldithiocarbamate; chlomethoxyfen; chloramben; chlorazifop-butyl, chlormesulon (ICI-A0051); chlorbromuron; chlorbufam; chlorfenac; chlorflurecol-methyl; chloridazon; chlorimuron ethyl; chlornitrofen; chlorotoluron; chloroxuron; chlorpropham; chlorsulfuron; chlorthal-dimethyl; chlorthiamid; cinmethylin; cinosulfuron; clethodim; clodinafop and its ester derivatives (e.g. clodinafop-propargyl); clomazone;
paragraphs.notes: A running semicolon-separated list of herbicide common names, code numbers and chemical names, alphabetical from acetochlor to clomazone, continuing onto the next page. Almost all of it is nomenclature rather than German prose; the only German in it is 'd.h.', 'und', 'z.B.', 'und dessen Esterderivate' and the German chemical names (essigsaeure, essigsaeuremethylester, Ammoniumsulfamat, 5-Fluor-2-phenyl-4H-3,1-benzoxazin-4-on, 2-Chlor-N,N-di-2-propenylacetamid, Diethyldithiocarbaminsaeure-2-chlorallylester), so zh and en differ only in those places. Transcribed as printed, including three oddities that are in the original and are not transcription errors: 'carbetamide' is printed between 'cafenstrole' and 'cafentrazone', breaking the alphabetical order; 'chlorazifop-butyl,' is followed by a comma where every other entry has a semicolon; and the code '(ICI-A0051)' is printed twice, once on cafentrazone and once on chlormesulon. Line-end hyphens inside chemical names ('(trifluoromethyl)-phenoxy', 'und -essigsaeuremethylester', '2-Chlor-N,N-di-2-propenylacetamid') are part of the names and are kept.
